q: The blue sky catastrophe (Shilnikov-Turaev) is a bifurcation where a stable periodic orbit disappears as its period goes to infinity. It occurs when the periodic orbit approaches:
opts: A saddle-node periodic orbit on an invariant torus (the orbit approaches another periodic orbit)
exp: Blue sky catastrophe (Turaev-Shilnikov 1995): a stable periodic orbit disappears as it approaches a saddle periodic orbit (creating a heteroclinic connection), with the period T → ∞ and amplitude remaining bounded (unlike homoclinic bifurcations where amplitude → 0). The orbit 'disappears into the blue sky'.
